summary: A tiny encoder-decoder Transformer in plain PyTorch, one short file per idea of the paper: scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, sinusoidal positional encoding, and the encoder and decoder stacks with residual connections and layer normalization. It trains on a toy sequence-reversal task on a laptop CPU in under a minute, so a learner can read every line, run it and watch attention learn.

milestones.title: Runnable skeleton
milestones.commit: build(project): set up a uv project with torch and a smoke test
milestones.deliverable: pyproject.toml (torch, pytest as a dev dependency), the tinyformer package with an empty __init__.py and a __main__.py that prints the config, tests/test_smoke.py.
milestones.done_when: `uv run python -m tinyformer` prints the config and `uv run pytest` passes.

milestones.title: Scaled dot-product attention
milestones.commit: feat(attention): add scaled dot-product attention with masking
milestones.deliverable: tinyformer/attention.py: attention(q, k, v, mask) computing softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))V, with padding and causal masks; tests for output shape, rows summing to 1 and masked positions getting zero weight.

milestones.title: Multi-head attention
milestones.deliverable: MultiHeadAttention in tinyformer/attention.py: project to h heads, attend in parallel, concatenate, project back; a test that it preserves the (batch, length, d_model) shape and respects the causal mask.
milestones.done_when: `uv run pytest tests/test_attention.py` passes with the new tests.

milestones.title: Positional encoding and the layers
milestones.commit: feat(model): add sinusoidal positions and encoder/decoder layers
milestones.deliverable: tinyformer/model.py: sinusoidal positional encoding, the position-wise feed-forward network, EncoderLayer and DecoderLayer (self-attention, cross-attention, each sublayer wrapped in a residual connection and layer norm).
milestones.done_when: `uv run pytest tests/test_model.py` passes: each layer keeps the input shape and a decoder position cannot see later positions.

milestones.title: The full Transformer
milestones.commit: feat(model): stack the layers into an encoder-decoder transformer
milestones.deliverable: Transformer in tinyformer/model.py: embeddings scaled by sqrt(d_model), N encoder and N decoder layers, a final linear layer to vocabulary logits; a tiny default config (d_model 64, 2 heads, 2 layers).
milestones.done_when: A forward pass on a random batch returns logits of shape (batch, target length, vocab) in `uv run pytest`.

milestones.title: Train on a toy task
milestones.commit: feat(train): train on sequence reversal and decode greedily
milestones.deliverable: tinyformer/train.py: a generated dataset of random digit sequences and their reversals, a training loop with Adam and cross-entropy, greedy decoding, and `python -m tinyformer train` printing the loss and a few decoded examples.
milestones.done_when: `uv run python -m tinyformer train` finishes on a CPU in under a minute and its decoded examples are mostly correct reversals.

milestones.title: Prove it learns
milestones.commit: test(train): check the model learns to reverse short sequences
milestones.deliverable: tests/test_train.py: a seeded run of a few hundred steps on length-6 sequences that asserts the final loss is well below the first one.
milestones.done_when: `uv run pytest` passes in under 30 seconds on a CPU.

milestones.title: Explain it
milestones.commit: docs: explain how to run it and which code is which idea
milestones.deliverable: README.md: how to install and run (uv sync, the train command, the tests), a table mapping each paper idea to its function and file, what was left out and why, and the milestone checklist ticked.
milestones.done_when: Every command in README.md runs as written on a fresh clone.

out_of_scope: Training on real translation data and BPE tokenization: the toy task shows the mechanism in seconds, real data would take hours.
Beam search and checkpoint averaging: greedy decoding is enough to see the model work.
Label smoothing and the warmup learning-rate schedule: named in the README as the next things to add, each a few lines.
Reproducing the paper's reported translation scores.
risks: A toy task can be solved without attention doing anything interesting: the README prints one attention map so the learner can see it align positions.
Post-norm training can be unstable even at this size: keep the learning rate small and the test seeded, and note pre-norm as the usual fix.
questions: Encoder-decoder as in the paper, or a decoder-only model (less code)? The plan follows the paper.
Should the training loop show an attention heatmap (adds matplotlib)? The plan prints it as text instead.
